10: # C4 Review
11: 
12: Review C4 architecture models for notation compliance, completeness, and common mistakes.
13: 
14: ## When to Use
15: 
16: - Reviewing a PR that modifies `architecture/workspace.dsl`
17: - Auditing an existing C4 model for quality
18: - Before publishing or sharing architecture diagrams
19: - After significant model changes to catch regressions
20: - When onboarding to understand if an existing model is trustworthy
21: 
22: ## Required Inputs
23: 
24: 1. Path to the Structurizr DSL workspace file (typically `architecture/workspace.dsl`)
25: 2. Optionally: the project's technology stack and deployment context for completeness checks
26: 
27: ## Workflow
28: 
29: ### Phase 1: Syntax Validation
30: 
31: Run structurizr/structurizr to catch syntax errors before manual review:
32: 
33: Run Structurizr with the most native OCI runtime available, written `$RUNTIME` below: `container` on Apple Silicon macOS (after `container system start`), `wslc` on Windows where available, otherwise `podman` (Docker works too). Pin a dated image tag rather than `latest`, which moves: a newer release can reject a model an older one accepted. On a Linux host with SELinux, add `:z` to the volume.
34: 
35: ```bash
36: $RUNTIME run --rm \
37:   -v "$(pwd):/work" \
38:   structurizr/structurizr:2026.09.19 validate -w /work/architecture/workspace.dsl
39: ```
40: 
41: Mount the project root (not just `architecture/`) so `!adrs` / `!docs` symlinks resolve.
42: 
43: If validation fails, fix syntax errors first. Do not proceed with review until the model parses cleanly.
44: 
45: ### Phase 2: Workspace Inspection
46: 
47: Run the `inspect` subcommand to surface Checkstyle-style violations (missing descriptions, duplicate names, duplicate view keys, duplicate relationship descriptions, etc.):
48: 
49: ```bash
50: $RUNTIME run --rm \
51:   -v "$(pwd):/work" \
52:   structurizr/structurizr:2026.09.19 inspect -w /work/architecture/workspace.dsl -s error,warning
53: ```
54: 
55: The exit code equals the number of violations. Severity levels can be tuned per element via `structurizr.inspection.*` workspace properties (`ignore`, `info`, `warning`, `error`).
56: 
57: ### Phase 3: Element Review (manual)
58: 
59: Check every element in the model against these criteria:
60: 
61: #### People/Actors
62: - [ ] Every person has a clear, specific name (not "User" unless truly generic)
63: - [ ] Every person has a description stating their role/goal
64: - [ ] No duplicate people representing the same role
65: - [ ] External vs internal actors are distinguished (via tags or naming)
66: 
67: #### Software Systems
68: - [ ] Your system has a name and description
69: - [ ] External systems are clearly identified (tagged "External" or similar)
70: - [ ] Each external system has a description explaining what it provides
71: - [ ] No system is modeled that should actually be a container (e.g., a database you own)
72: - [ ] System names are unique and unambiguous
73: 
74: #### Containers
75: - [ ] Every container represents a **runtime boundary** (separately running process or data store)
76: - [ ] No libraries, modules, or packages modeled as containers
77: - [ ] Every container has a technology specified
78: - [ ] Every container has a meaningful description (not just restating the name)
79: - [ ] Database containers use the "Database" tag for cylinder shape
80: - [ ] No containers that should be external systems (services you don't own/deploy)
81: 
82: #### Components (if present)
83: - [ ] Components represent architecturally significant groupings, not just folder structure
84: - [ ] Every component has technology specified
85: - [ ] Components are within a single container (not spanning containers)
86: - [ ] The component diagram adds genuine value (if not, recommend removing it)
87: 
88: ### Phase 4: Relationship Review
89: 
90: Check every relationship:
91: 
92: #### Labels
93: - [ ] Every relationship has a label describing **intent** (what is communicated, not just "uses")
94: - [ ] Labels match the arrow direction (source does X **to** destination)
95: - [ ] No vague labels: flag "Uses", "Connects to", "Interacts with", "Communicates with"
96: 
97: Suggest specific alternatives for vague labels:
98: | Vague | Ask | Better Example |
99: |-------|-----|----------------|
100: | "Uses" | What does it use it for? | "queries order history from" |
101: | "Connects to" | What data flows? | "sends email notifications via" |
102: | "Interacts with" | What's the interaction? | "submits search queries to" |
103: | "Communicates with" | What's communicated? | "publishes order events to" |
104: 
105: #### Technology
106: - [ ] Inter-container relationships specify protocol/technology (e.g., "JSON/HTTPS", "SQL/TCP", "gRPC", "AMQP")
107: - [ ] Intra-container relationships (component-to-component) may omit technology
108: - [ ] Person-to-container relationships specify the interface technology (e.g., "HTTPS", "WebSocket")
109: 
110: #### Direction
111: - [ ] Arrows point in the direction of dependency or data flow
112: - [ ] No bidirectional relationships (split into two if needed)
113: - [ ] Implied relationships make sense (e.g., user → container implies user → system)
114:

118: 
119: #### System Context View
120: - [ ] Exists (required for all projects)
121: - [ ] Shows the system at center with all users and external systems
122: - [ ] Uses `include *` or explicitly includes all relevant elements
123: - [ ] Has a descriptive title
124: - [ ] Does NOT include internal containers or components
125: - [ ] Does NOT include technology details (keep it non-technical)
126:

128: - [ ] Exists (required for all projects)
129: - [ ] Shows all containers within the system boundary
130: - [ ] Includes people and external systems that interact with containers
131: - [ ] Has a descriptive title
132: - [ ] Does NOT include deployment details (clustering, load balancing, replication)
133: - [ ] Does NOT show components (those belong in component views)
134: 
135: #### Component View (if present)
136: - [ ] Scoped to a single container
137: - [ ] Only created for containers where internal structure matters
138: - [ ] Not just mirroring the code's package structure
139: 
140: #### Dynamic View (if present)
141: - [ ] Clearly scoped to a specific feature or use case
142: - [ ] Interactions are numbered in sequence
143: - [ ] Includes only elements involved in the specific flow
144: 
145: #### Deployment View (if present)
146: - [ ] Scoped to a specific environment (production, staging, etc.)
147: - [ ] Shows deployment nodes, not just containers
148: - [ ] Infrastructure nodes (load balancers, DNS, firewalls) are included where relevant
149: 
150: ### Phase 6: Style Review
151: 
152: - [ ] People use `shape Person`
153: - [ ] Databases use `shape Cylinder`
154: - [ ] Colors are consistent across diagram types

156: - [ ] Tags are used for styling (not hardcoded per element)
157: - [ ] Consider color blindness — don't rely on color alone to convey meaning
158:

160: 
161: - [ ] All known users/personas are represented
162: - [ ] All external system integrations are modeled
163: - [ ] All major containers are present (web app, API, database, queues, etc.)
164: - [ ] Relationships cover all known communication paths

166: - [ ] System context and container views exist at minimum

170: - [ ] `!identifiers hierarchical` is used (recommended for non-trivial models)

172: - [ ] Tags are used consistently for element types

175: - [ ] `!docs` directive points to documentation (if applicable)
